PullRequest.Title: Keep NLS data and owned regex literals ASCII
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Keep generated NLS JavaScript and the remaining directly owned regex literals ASCII.

- Add a small NLS-only serializer and use it for active `build/next` output, legacy extraction, and translated JavaScript catalogs.
- Preserve JSON catalog bytes, decoded message values, language IDs, missing-translation fallback, and legal headers.
- Escape eight owned regexes in workspace-picker labels, Codex snapshot-image matching, search-result parsing, Copilot file-tree depth calculation, and Markdown notebook slugification.
- Remove the now-redundant notebook Unicode exemption.

## Why

Esbuild retains raw Unicode in regex literals, and plain `JSON.stringify` retains Unicode in generated NLS source. Characters above U+00FF can force a wide script representation during loading.

The NLS change is distinct from #336098: that pass intentionally does not rewrite runtime string literals. Escaping at the NLS serialization boundary preserves the actual localized strings, including astral characters and isolated surrogate values.

In the audited release catalogs, the generated JavaScript grows by only 691 bytes (desktop) and 548 bytes (web), while all 24,742 / 21,459 message values remain identical. No new end-to-end latency improvement is claimed by this source-cleanup PR.

## Validation

- Client transpilation and scoped type checks passed.
- **73 targeted tests passed:** 50 Electron, 6 Copilot, and 17 NLS/source-map/localization tests.
- Hygiene and direct lint checks passed, including Copilot's own lint command.
- NLS tests cover every UTF-16 code unit, astral/isolated surrogates, literal escape text, missing translations, primary/mirror output, and exact JSON catalog preservation.
- Differential checks passed 525,168 regex cases and 65,564 slug cases per Node/Electron runtime; regex flags, captures, groups, and `lastIndex` were preserved.
- Actual Markdown-notebook and search-result browser bundles were checked. Remaining dependency-origin regexes are the separate #336098 scope.

The changed regexes are local matching/replacement expressions; their reflected source spelling changes, but runtime strings and raw templates are not rewritten.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build/next NLS finalization for desktop bundles
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After esbuild completes, finalizeNLS must finish before output JavaScript is post-processed and written. The changed serialization is therefore on the build critical path, but it is a single linear pass over the collected message JSON per output directory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create two output directories and write four NLS files to each directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two mkdir calls followed by eight writes for the production call in build/next/index.ts; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same directories and files were created and written; nls.messages.js used JSON.stringify directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: finalizeNLS is awaited before bundle post-processing proceeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: 24,742 collected messages, emitted to the primary output and the out-build compatibility mirror; effective multiplicity is two serializations because the existing flatMap builds one JavaScript payload per directory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Directory creation is serialized; the eight existing file writes for two directories run in one Promise.all. The diff does not change write concurrency or add a limiter need.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used before or after the diff. Both cold and warm builds regenerate these catalogs; output-directory mirroring already caused JSON serialization per destination.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added replace scans the JSON string and can allocate a replacement string, while call placement and two-directory cardinality are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalog byte size and build-machine throughput vary, but only sparse non-ASCII matches expand; the extra regex scan remains linear and bounded to generated catalog size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra bounded build-time scan/allocation adds no boundary calls or concurrency and is small relative to collection, sorting, multiple existing JSON serializations, and eight filesystem writes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Legacy compilation and localized Monaco catalog generation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The legacy compiler emits one base nls.messages.js after compilation, and the editor localization task synchronously reads translation data and builds one JavaScript catalog for each configured language before the gulp stream completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check for and synchronously read each language pack's main.i18n.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one exists check and one read for each of 13 configured languages; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same checks, reads, parsing, and emitted files occurred; generated JavaScript embedded JSON.stringify output directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads and parsing happen synchronously before each localized output is queued.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit generated NLS metadata and message files through the gulp stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One set of base files plus one localized JavaScript catalog per configured language; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same files were emitted with unescaped non-ASCII JSON source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The stream must complete before the build task finishes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One base catalog plus 13 configured localized catalogs, each proportional to the NLS key/message count after grouping by module.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Languages are processed synchronously with forEach; existing translation reads and output queueing remain serialized. The diff does not increase language count or alter scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No in-process cache is used; each build regenerates catalogs. Missing translation files retain the existing fallback behavior and still produce one catalog per language.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: serialization now adds a regex scan per catalog, but all filesystem cardinality and serialization grouping remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Build host speed and localization sparsity vary. The added scan is O(total emitted catalog bytes), but the PR evidence indicates only hundreds of bytes of expansion in release catalogs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded extra scan does not create fan-out or meaningfully alter the existing build critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hot runtime text parsing and rendering using the escaped regex literals
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Search-result parsing runs synchronously on document parse/decorate paths; notebook slugification runs during Markdown render per heading/link; Copilot file-tree depth runs once per generated tree line; workspace action label cleanup runs per browse action; Codex legacy snapshot matching runs per replayed turn chunk.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Search-result document lines and elision markers, notebook headings/anchor links, generated file-tree lines, provider browse actions, and replay text chunks respectively. Effective cardinality is unchanged because every edited regex denotes the same characters and match structure as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All these operations remain synchronous in their existing local loops; no new task, queue, fan-out, or parallel boundary is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Search results retain their version/URI parse cache; notebook slug counters reset per render; the other paths remain uncached as before. The source spelling changes do not alter keys or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: each diff only replaces a literal Unicode code point in a regex with its equivalent Unicode escape, preserving flags, captures, anchoring, and caller loops.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Input sizes vary, especially search-result documents and generated file trees, but regex engine work and iteration counts are semantically unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Runtime algorithms, match cardinality, synchronous work, allocations, and boundary behavior are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files. The only added work is a bounded build-time JSON-string regex scan; runtime regex edits are source-equivalent. No high-confidence, actionable performance regression or proven shipped regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
